summary: Retest of M2-S02 (permission sets and permission set groups for Tier 1, Tier 2 and Billing) after rebuild #3, the F-60 repair that added 7 fieldPermissions to Case_Agent_Core for the standard Case fields the agent persona writes. Ran the always-on xml and manifest checks plus all three declared checker acceptance tests. All 8 XML files parsed, package.xml is consistent with the artefacts in both directions, and check_permission_set_architecture.py (build scope), check_permission_set_group_composition.py (step scope) and check_access_model.py (step scope) each exited 0. check_access_model.py newly carries PSVP-FLS-01/PSVP-FLS-02 (added today) and reports one WARN-severity, non-blocking finding on Case_Agent_Core's EmailMessage grant, which is the residual explained in artefacts/M2-S02/deploy-order.md and does not fail the checker's own exit code. check-outputs confirmed all 8 declared outputs exist, are non-empty and parse. No manual acceptance tests are declared on this step. Status set to tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran to completion, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly; no checker was missing, no manifest exclusion was needed, and check-outputs passed clean. The one WARN finding is non-blocking (checker's own blocking:0) and is a documented, explained residual rather than an unresolved gap, so it does not pull confidence down per the Step 7 rubric.

process_observations.observation: The F-60 repair is narrowly scoped: only Case_Agent_Core's fieldPermissions and description changed (7 fields added, description reworded to 193 chars); Case_Tier1, Case_Tier2, Case_Billing and all three PermissionSetGroup files are byte-identical to rebuild #2, matching what artefacts/M2-S02/deploy-order.md's Rebuild #3 section claims.

check_access_model.py's new PSVP-FLS-01 rule cleared cleanly on Case's Create/Edit grant on Case_Agent_Core after the repair (score rose from 94 pre-edit to 97 post-edit, per deploy-order.md's own before/after capture); the fix targeted exactly the flagged object.
No PermissionSet or PermissionSetGroup file under artefacts/M2-S02/ carries a viewAllRecords or modifyAllRecords element set to true.

check_access_model.py's PSVP-FLS-01 finding on Case_Agent_Core's EmailMessage Create/Edit grant remains open after this rebuild. It is non-blocking and already named in deploy-order.md as a deliberate non-fix pending either a compose-UI step or a clarification answer naming which standard EmailMessage fields a reply populates -- not invented here, but it is real residual risk sitting in front of the milestone gate.

deploy-order.md sits under artefacts/M2-S02/ but is not named in any of the step's five declared acceptance_tests, so it is not covered by the xml, manifest or checker checks; per this agent's brief it is reported as undeclared rather than failed. This was also true on the rebuild-#2 retest and remains unchanged.

citations.used_for: Section 5 governs acceptance-test types, runner dispatch, the literal-command rule, checker scope, the deny-list, and the always-on xml/manifest checks this run followed; also the note that a checker's exit-policy form may distinguish blocking findings from advisory ones, which is why PSVP-FLS-01's WARN does not fail the run.
Section 4 step-type table confirms 'access' is a metadata step type, so the always-on manifest check must fail rather than skip if no package.xml existed.
